summary: installShutdown registers SIGINT and SIGTERM listeners, which turns off Node's default exit-on-signal. Its once-guard then ignores every trigger after the first. The teardown it starts is bridge.shutdown() -> releaseAll() -> await plugin.disconnect(), and nothing bounds that wait. A backend whose disconnect hangs therefore leaves a bridge that no signal short of SIGKILL ends, and an orphaned bridge whose parent died lingers forever — the exact failure the installShutdown comment says the wiring prevents. A shutdown that rejects also exits 0 (.finally), hiding the failure.
failure: I ran runBackendCli under vite-node with a FakePlugin whose disconnect() never resolves. After 'bridge up' I sent SIGTERM, SIGTERM, then SIGINT: stderr showed 'disconnect called' and the process was still alive 6 s later. It needed SIGKILL.
remediation: In runBackendCli's onShutdown, arm a teardown deadline: setTimeout(() => process.exit(1), N).unref(). Exit 1 if shutdown rejects: bridge.shutdown().then(() => exit(0), () => exit(1)). Let installShutdown accept an optional onRepeat hook that force-exits on a second signal, keeping once-only teardown for the stdin end/close pair.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: bridge.shutdown() from createStdioBridge, which ends in releaseAll's `await attempt(() => plugin.disconnect())` with no timeout
remediationCheck.newlyRejects: a backend whose legitimate disconnect takes longer than the deadline is killed with exit 1 instead of finishing
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: none found. shutdown.test.ts SEQUENCES assert teardown runs exactly once, which an onRepeat hook used only for force-exit leaves unchanged. backend-cli.test.ts only covers parseArgs.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: A disconnect that hangs still leaks the backend-side session (the server does not see a clean close). The fix bounds process lifetime; it does not fix the plugin.
remediationCheck.interleavings: A signal followed by stdin EOF calls onShutdown once, then a repeat that is not force-exited (stdin events are not repeats of intent). Signal then signal: force-exit. If the deadline fires while shutdown resolves, exit is called twice and the first call wins — both paths are exits.

The agent calls parley_fetch_recent and gets [M]. The write then returns, and M is emitted as a <channel> event anyway. pushes == ["M"] after fetched == ["M"]. remediation: In route(), after `await opts.own.settled()` and the own.has check, add `if (opts.handed.has(m.topic, m.backendMsgId)) return;` before routing and marking. That way a message a read handed over while the route waited is not emitted again.

summary: ReadStateStore.set assigns the in-memory cursor before flush(). When flush throws (EACCES, ENOSPC, rename onto a directory), the tool call fails, but get() already returns the new cursor. summary: assertTrustProxy probes express's compiled predicate at hop Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. summary: Rotation deletes the presented refresh token (revokeGrant), so a retired token is indistinguishable from an unknown one. If a refresh token is stolen and the attacker rotates first, the legitimate client's next refresh just gets invalid_grant. The attacker's grant stays alive for up to 30 days, and the owner's only lever is a restart: re-consent mints a NEW grant and does not touch the stolen one. The OAuth 2.1 rotation model expects reuse of a retired token to revoke the active grant.

summary: connectReader never looks at the RESP error the server emitted during a reader's handshake. node-redis surfaces a refused handshake as a ReconnectStrategyError carrying our own 'cannot reach' text, so serverRefusal(err) never matches it. blockingRead's catch (line 267) then returns [] at once, which breaks the README promise that a refusal 'fails the call with a labelled error rather than being reported as an empty long poll' and that a long poll 'never comes back early with an empty page'. Core reads that as a timed-out poll and re-opens a doomed reader every nap. subscribe() on a new topic rejects with "parley-redis: parley-redis: cannot reach 127.0.0.1:16399 (connect_timeout_ms=5000) (topic …)", sending the operator to the network while the server answered WRONGPASS. post() keeps succeeding, so nothing else in the process surfaces the fault.

Otherwise throw isPluginError(err) ? err : pluginError(unreachable(url, connectTimeoutMs)). That also removes the doubled prefix (separate finding).

summary: When a subscribe reader's connection drops and node-redis' internal reconnect is refused (rotated password, revoked ACL), every xRead rejects with ClientOfflineError. That only holds if the entry is cleared on 'ready', so a refusal from an earlier, already-recovered outage cannot stop a healthy loop later.

summary: fetchRecent forwards args.limit straight into `LIMIT $2` with no validation and no ceiling. After the addressing change, core sends cfg.catchup.limit (z.number().int().positive(), no upper bound) on EVERY post as guardLimit, not only at start-up.

Each tells the caller a retry will succeed. Through config: catchup.limit: 1e20 (passes core's zod) with on_start true makes the bridge fail to start with 22003. With on_start false, every parley_post fails, because unreadBeforePost passes limit: deps.guardLimit. With catchup.limit: 1_000_000, every guarded post on a never-read topic SELECTs up to 1M rows into memory, and core then keeps 1000. The 'parley-postgres:' prefix lets serverRefused pass it through unchanged.

summary: startSubscription captures `listener = await this.ensureListener()`, awaits a pool tail read, and only then sends LISTEN on that captured client. If the listener connection drops in that window, the LISTEN goes to a dead client and subscribe rejects. core's startPushLoop rethrows that, so the bridge fails to come up. The ensureListener JSDoc says it prevents exactly this: 'handed the dead client it is guaranteed to fail, and core's push loop rethrows that, so the whole bridge fails to come up'. A replacement is already in flight (listenerPromise points at it), but the subscribe never asks for it.
failure: Reproduced: subscribe(a), then pg_terminate_backend(listener pid) during subscribe(b)'s COALESCE(MAX(seq)) read. subscribe(b) rejects with 'parley-postgres: could not establish the live path for topic 'b-…' — Client has encountered a connection error and is not queryable'. A retry 1.5 s later succeeds and push then delivers. So the failure is purely the window, and at start-up it aborts the bridge.
remediation: In startSubscription, after the tail read, re-acquire the listener (`const current = await this.ensureListener()`) and LISTEN on that, not on the client captured before the await. If acquireListen rejects and `this.listener !== listener` (the client was replaced or is reconnecting), retry once against `await this.ensureListener()` within LISTENER_WAIT_MS before failing.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: reconnectListener's synchronous `this.listenerPromise = replacement;` on 'end', so ensureListener() after the drop returns the replacement; acquireListen's `if (this.listens.get(channel) === entry) this.listens.delete(channel);` so the failed first attempt leaves no stale entry for the re-LISTEN loop
remediationCheck.newlyAccepts: a subscribe whose listener dropped mid-call and was replaced within LISTENER_WAIT_MS, which today rejects
remediationCheck.testsThatWouldFail: none found. I looked at listener-blackout.test.ts, where the 'subscribe … during the blackout' rows declare outcomes for calls issued AFTER the drop, and at subscribe-race.test.ts 'shared LISTEN fails rejects for every caller'. That row fails the LISTEN on a live client; if it does so by marking the client dead, a retry may change its declared arm.
remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: If the replacement never lands within the bound, subscribe still rejects, which is correct. The retry LISTEN can race reconnectListener's own re-LISTEN of listens.keys(), which costs a duplicate LISTEN (idempotent in PostgreSQL).
remediationCheck.interleavings: (1) Drop before the tail read: ensureListener returns the replacement, fine. (2) Drop during the tail read: the re-acquire after the read returns the replacement. (3) Drop during the LISTEN: retry path. (4) Two subscribes to different topics both retrying: each LISTENs its own channel on the replacement, and the reconnect loop's snapshot may include either, which is a duplicate LISTEN and harmless. (5) disconnect during the retry: the existing stopped/epoch check after acquireListen still rejects and releases.

summary: Removing the epoch condition from `if (epoch === this.epoch) this.reconnecting = false;` is caught ONLY by lifecycle.test.ts's regex census ('every teardown guard in the source is represented by a row above'). Without bail, 1070 tests pass and only that census fails. Tracing shows why no behavioural test can catch it: reconnectListener is invoked only from a listener 'end' handler gated on `this.listener === client`, and while a successor lifecycle's loop runs, no adopted client exists that could emit a second 'end'. So the guard defends an interleaving that cannot occur, and the census forces it to stay. The same holds for adoptListener's `!this.starting.delete(client)` condition: disconnect() always bumps epoch, so the condition is implied by `epoch !== this.epoch`, and the mutant survives all 1071 tests.

If it is not, delete the dead condition and drop the census count by one. Replace the TEARDOWN_GUARD_SITES census with per-site behavioural rows, per CLAUDE.md's 'assert the invariant, not the layout'.

The alternative is a seam-level fix in core: push-loop route yields one macrotask before own.has(), or OwnPosts keeps waiting for an in-flight write whose result has not arrived. summary: Once `hello` arrives, the only things that can trigger a redial are the socket's 'close' event and a `disconnect` envelope. There is no ping/pong, idle-read timer or keepalive. The link is receive-only (it sends only acks, and only in reply to inbound frames), so a connection that dies silently — NAT/LB idle expiry, Wi-Fi handoff, laptop suspend — never produces a close. The live path then goes dead for the life of the process with no error anywhere.
failure: Reproduced. I put a TCP proxy in front of the fake's websocket (fake.setWsUrl) and subscribed. One post was delivered live. remediation: In openSocket, once `hello` is seen, arm a per-socket heartbeat. Call ws.ping() every interval, and refresh a lastHeard stamp on 'pong', 'ping' and 'message'. If lastHeard is older than a bound, call ws.terminate(). Clear the interval in the socket's 'close' handler. terminate() emits 'close', so the existing helloSeen branch (noteConnectionEnded + reconnect) does the redial, and no second redial path is created.

summary: A record write that fails partway (ENOSPC after some bytes) leaves an unterminated fragment. The process recovers: tornTail starts the next line fresh, and the next post succeeds and its cursor works. But the fragment stays in the append-only file. At the next load it counts as a dropped line (store.ts:184, `lost = dropped || ...`), so the store mints a fresh identity and refuses every cursor any agent holds. The burned sequence was never issued to anyone.
failure: Reproduced. post 'seed' -> fetchRecent gives nextCursor C. The next appendFileSync writes half its bytes and throws ENOSPC, so post 'subject' rejects. post 'after' succeeds, and fetchRecent(since C) = ['after'] in-process. Then disconnect + new plugin on the same store_path: fetchRecent(since C) rejects with "cursor '<old>.1' ... was issued by a different observed-message store", and stderr says "did not load whole — a damaged or torn line could not be loaded. Minted a fresh store identity". Every agent's saved cursor is refused after one transient disk-full that cost no issued cursor.
remediation: Remove the fragment at the moment of failure instead of leaving it for the loader. In StoreFile.write, read `fstatSync(fd).size` before appendFileSync. In the catch, try `ftruncateSync(fd, sizeBefore)`; set tornTail only if that truncate itself throws. An alternative that stays inside the append-only discipline: set a `dirty` flag on write failure and have the next successful ObservedStore.append call `file.compact(journalText())`, which rewrites the file from memory without the fragment and keeps the current epoch.

remediationCheck.reliesOn: StoreFile.write's catch branch `this.tornTail = true; throw err;` (store-file.ts:522-525). The fd is opened O_APPEND by openAppend(), so after a truncate the next write lands at the new end. The single-writer StoreLock means no other process appends between the fstat and the truncate.
remediationCheck.newlyAccepts: A restart after an in-process write failure keeps the store identity and answers held cursors.

remediationCheck.hidesOrFixes: If ftruncateSync itself fails (EIO, read-only remount), the fragment stays and the restart still re-mints. That residual needs the compaction variant or stays as today.
remediationCheck.interleavings: Single writer per file (StoreLock). Within the process, post's ingest and the poll loop's deliver are both synchronous calls into append, so no second append can run between the failed write and its truncate.

summary: The conformance `concurrentPost` fixture is restated in 8 packages: discord, matrix, nats, postgres, redis, slack and xmpp conformance.test.ts, plus zulip/test/harness.ts. It is the same 17-line body, differing only in the plugin constructor and connect config. All 8 carry the same defect: the writers are connected with `await Promise.all(...)` before the `try`, so when one writer's connect rejects, the writers that already connected are never disconnected. Their sockets and timers leak into the rest of the vitest worker. sqlite's copy (forked children) is the only different one.
failure: Trace: if writer k of N rejects in `p.connect(...)`, `Promise.all` rejects and the `try { ... } finally { plugins.map(p => p.disconnect()) }` is never entered. The fulfilled writers 0..k-1 stay connected, with live sockets and NATS/Redis readers that keep event-loop handles open, which can surface later as hangs or cross-case interference attributed to some other case.
remediation: Have @sharptrick/parley-conformance export `concurrentWriters(open: () => Promise<BackendPlugin>)`, which opens with Promise.allSettled, disconnects every fulfilled writer on any failure, and owns the post loop. Each fixture then shrinks to `concurrentPost: concurrentWriters(() => connected(new RedisPlugin(), cfg))`, keeping matrix's and xmpp's pre-warm as a prologue.
